concepts.def: Angle measured up from horizontal to an object.
Angle measured down from horizontal to an object.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An angle of elevation looks up; an angle of depression looks down.

Ladder example: a 5 m ladder leans against a wall. The angle of elevation from the ground is 60°. How high up the wall does it reach?

The wall height is the opposite side; the ladder is the hypotenuse. Use SOH: height = 5 × sin 60° ≈ 5 × 0.866 ≈ 4.33 m.

Shadow example: a tree casts a 10 m shadow. The sun's elevation is 45°. Height = 10 × tan 45° = 10 × 1 = 10 m.

A bearing is the direction of one point from another, measured clockwise from North, always written with 3 digits.

• North = 000°
• East = 090°
• South = 180°
• West = 270°

Worked idea: a boat sails on a bearing of 060° for 8 km. How far East has it travelled? The journey makes a right-angled triangle with North; East is the opposite side to the 60° bearing. East distance = 8 × sin 60° ≈ 6.93 km.

For non-calculator papers, learn these by heart:

sin 30° = 1/2   cos 60° = 1/2
sin 45° = cos 45° = √2 / 2 ≈ 0.71
tan 45° = 1
sin 60° = cos 30° = √3 / 2 ≈ 0.87
tan 30° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.58   tan 60° = √3 ≈ 1.73

Quick check: sin² θ + cos² θ should always equal 1. e.g. (1/2)² + (√3/2)² = 1/4 + 3/4 = 1. ✓
